nodes.content: Develop a semantic parser that generalizes variable binding and quantifier scope to unseen compositions without sacrificing familiar-construction accuracy.
requirements: Achieve ≥90% logical-form exact match on withheld scope–binding combinations with matched vocabulary and length distributions.
Keep familiar-construction exact-match accuracy within two percentage points of an equally sized supervised baseline.

nodes.content: Train a typed de Bruijn-indexed grammar decoder on a fixed-size mix of synthetic scope–binding recombinations and original examples.
Does synthetic recombination improve binding across nested quantifiers without distorting scope choices in familiar constructions?
A 1:1 synthetic–original mix will yield ≥90% withheld scope–binding exact match and ≤2-point familiar accuracy loss versus equal-sized supervision.
Build vocabulary- and length-matched withheld scope–binding splits; train equal-sized mixed and supervised decoders; compare familiar and withheld exact match.
Construct ScopeBind-v1 splits withholding nested-quantifier/binding pairings while matching vocabulary and utterance and logical-form length distributions.
ScopeBind-v1 contains training, familiar-test, and withheld-pairing test splits, plus vocabulary and length-matching audit tables.
Audit ScopeBind-v1 vocabulary and length matching; train equal-sized mixed and supervised decoders; compare withheld and familiar exact match against thresholds.
On ScopeBind-v1, mixed decoding achieved 92.1% withheld exact match versus 71.4% supervised; familiar exact match was 95.0% versus 96.2%.
Adopt the 1:1 mixed typed decoder: 92.1% withheld exact match exceeds 90%, with familiar accuracy only 1.2 points below baseline.
Run equal-budget ScopeBind-v1 ablations of de Bruijn indexing, type constraints, and recombination; score withheld and familiar exact match.
ScopeBind-v1 withheld exact match: full 92.1%; without recombination 74.8%, typing 86.3%, or de Bruijn indexing 82.7%; familiar remained ≥95.0%.
Typed de Bruijn decoding alone, without recombination, will achieve ≥90% withheld and ≥95% familiar exact match.
Retrain the no-recombination typed decoder on five matched ScopeBind-v1 resplits; test 90% withheld and 95% familiar exact-match thresholds.
On five ScopeBind-v1 resplits, no-recombination averaged 90.4% withheld and 95.3% familiar exact match; the original withheld score was 74.8%.
Retain recombination pending split-variance analysis: no-recombination meets thresholds on resplits but fails the original withheld split.
Use a span-based compositional parser with explicit binder environments and a contrastive scope reranker trained on minimal pairs.
Can minimal-pair scope reranking generalize to withheld binder configurations without changing correct familiar-construction parses?
Binder-environment parsing plus contrastive reranking will reach ≥90% ScopeBind-v1 withheld exact match and ≤2-point familiar loss versus equal-sized supervision.
Train equal-budget binder-environment span parsers with and without minimal-pair reranking; compare ScopeBind-v1 withheld and familiar exact match to supervision.
On ScopeBind-v1, reranking raised withheld exact match from 84.3% to 88.6%, below 90%; familiar scored 95.1% versus 96.2% supervision.
Train a CCG parser with lexical lambda templates and explicit quantifier-raising rules, using familiar-example rehearsal.
Can CCG quantifier raising recover withheld nested binder scopes while rehearsal preserves familiar scope preferences?
Fit equal-budget CCG parsers with and without quantifier raising and familiar-example rehearsal; score ScopeBind-v1 withheld and familiar exact match.
Implement CCG lambda templates and quantifier-raising rules; train equal-budget variants with and without raising or familiar-example rehearsal on ScopeBind-v1.
CCG-Scope-v1 provides lambda-template grammar, quantifier-raising rules, and matched-budget checkpoints with and without raising or familiar-example rehearsal.
Score CCG-Scope-v1 checkpoints on ScopeBind-v1 withheld and familiar splits; compare raising and rehearsal ablations against 90% and two-point thresholds.
On ScopeBind-v1, CCG-Scope-v1 scored 91.3% withheld and 95.4% familiar exact match; without raising, withheld dropped to 83.1%.
Evaluate CCG-Scope-v1 without rehearsal on ScopeBind-v1; compare familiar exact-match retention and withheld scope–binding accuracy against the full model.
Across five ScopeBind-v1 resplits, rehearsal averaged 88.7% withheld exact match versus 90.5% without; familiar scores were 95.4% versus 95.6%.
Retain CCG quantifier raising but drop rehearsal: across resplits, withheld exact match rises from 88.7% to 90.5% without familiar loss.
Factor parsing into predicate structure and scope–binding decisions, then solve binding constraints symbolically with familiar-construction calibration.
Does symbolic binder resolution transfer across withheld scope combinations when predicate parsing and familiar scope calibration are learned separately?
Factorized parsing with symbolic resolution will achieve ≥90% withheld exact match and ≤2-point familiar loss against equal-sized supervision.
Train equal-budget factorized and supervised parsers on ScopeBind-v1; test withheld and familiar exact match with symbolic binding enabled and disabled.
On ScopeBind-v1, symbolic resolution scored 91.8% withheld but 92.9% familiar exact match versus 96.2% supervised.
Test gold-predicate and recalibrated-scope variants on ScopeBind-v1; compare withheld and familiar exact match against 90% and 94.2%.
On ScopeBind-v1, learned scope recalibration achieved 90.7% withheld and 94.6% familiar exact match, versus 91.8%/92.9% uncalibrated.
Keep symbolic resolution only with learned scope recalibration: it meets both thresholds, unlike the uncalibrated parser’s 3.3-point familiar deficit.
Train an alpha-renaming-equivariant graph decoder with scope-swap augmentation and a familiar-example consistency loss.
Can alpha-renaming equivariance distinguish binder identities in novel scope arrangements without disrupting familiar logical forms?
Equivariant graph decoding with scope swaps will exceed 90% withheld exact match while staying within two familiar-accuracy points of supervision.
Generate valid scope-swap pairs, train equal-budget equivariant and non-equivariant decoders, and score ScopeBind-v1 exact match plus alpha-renaming consistency.
Generate type-checked ScopeBind-v1 scope-swap pairs and train equal-budget equivariant graph decoders with familiar-example consistency loss.
EquiScope-v1 contains type-checked scope-swap pairs, graph-decoder checkpoints, and alpha-renaming consistency evaluation scripts.
Evaluate EquiScope-v1 against equal-budget non-equivariant decoding on ScopeBind-v1 withheld and familiar exact match and alpha-renaming consistency.
On ScopeBind-v1, EquiScope-v1 achieved 91.6% withheld and 95.0% familiar exact match versus 85.2%/95.6% non-equivariant; alpha-renaming consistency reached 98.4%.
Advance EquiScope-v1: withheld exact match exceeds 90%, and familiar accuracy trails equal-budget supervision by only 1.2 points.
